[spoiler=Operation External Fortress]

OPERATION: EXTERNAL FORTRESS
DATE: XX/XX/XXXX
OPERATION STATUS: ALL GOALS COMPLETED
ISLANDS SECURED: 16
DEAD OR WOUNDED: 19 LA TROOPS, ~170 VARIOUS NATIVES (CIVILIAN AND MILITIA)
AMOUNT OF SETTLERS GIVEN LAND: 250,000
AWARDS DISTRIBUTED: 85,000 CAMPAIGN MEDALS,  14 MEDAL OF BLOOD, 5 FALLEN WARRIOR MEDALS, 3 EXCELLENT AVIATOR MEDALS, + 800 VARIOUS
----------------------------------------------------------------
OBJECT OF INTEREST: PERSONAL MESSAGES VETTED BY SEGER INTELLIGENCE COMMAND
NAME OF WRITER: DAVID XXXXXXX
CURRENT STATUS: XXXXXXX
----------------------------------------------------------------
MESSAGE #1
Dear Ma,
Everything is going well so far. A few of the National Guard guys got sea sick, but thankfully we landed before one of them fainted from dehydration. Were working on setting up a small runway right next to the beach so some of the SLT planes weve been allocated can land and get us some armor in case there are locals that decide to put up a fight. Jeffry stuffed some canteens of good whisky into his rucksack, so were sitting good right now, apart from a good few bites of steak. 

Some helicopters dropped by to survey the island and had to refuel a few minutes ago. Hopefully this island isnt inhabited, but if it is, they are either on the other side of deaf, because these engineers with their bulldozers are loud as hell.

The animals are nothing special, same with the plants, but they do have a species of butterfly I think youd like. I found one dead in my tent after I woke up two days ago, so I decided to preserve it, then get on the ship to use the laminator in the officers hall (after trading a lieutenant some of the whisky to use it.) Looks like those science labs were good for something! 

Love, David.

INSIDE THE ENVELOPE, IS A LAMINATED PINK AND YELLOW BUTTERFLY.
MESSAGE STATUS: APPROVED AND SHIPPED
-----------------------------------------------------------------
MESSAGE #2
Hey Ma,
Hope you enjoyed the butterfly! Anyway, we finished the runway yesterday. Its been flights in and out nonstop to keep us supplied with building materials. Ive never seen so much rebar in my life! I also got to ride on one of the patrol helicopters I told you about, and the only sight of civilization we saw was a small coastal village on the south of the island. About 35 buildings of stone and wood, and I doubt no more than 50-70 could live there. A few of them were staring up at us, and a few of them seemed to have old muskets or something of the sort, I just hope we dont have to kill any of them.

I also enjoyed your little package! The chocolate was nice, and the jerky is absolutely heavenly when I have to stand guard! Oh yes, and Jeffry says thanks for the apple juice for his whisky! I wish I could share more, but were getting prepped to hop in the armor and go visit that village tomorrow. Hopefully it all goes well, and we dont have to complicate things. 

Love, David (and Jeffry too)
MESSAGE STATUS: APPROVED AND SHIPPED
-----------------------------------------------------------------

MESSAGE #3
Greetings from the hospital!
I'm sorry if I worried you at all in my last letter, or if I do in this one too. I took a musket shot to the arm, but Jeffry got a musket afterwards for me as a souvenir! Anyhow, time to explain to you what happened, seeing as I have nothing else to do in this hospital bed.

We rolled up to the village near about noon, and got out about half a mile away. We walked the rest of the way there, along with our AFVs. When we did get there, we had a translator who seemed to somewhat speak the language, so that was better than nothing. We exchanged some goods like candy from our rations and watches, you know, little commodities, for handmade knives or stuff like fresh mangos or pottery. One officer even traded three large bottles of vodka for a wonderful hide tapestry! 

Problem was when I had to take a piss, so I decided to walk away from the village for a bit. I may have accidentally walked onto their graveyard  for their leaders, and in their religion, thats a crime punishable by death for outsiders( (or that's how the translator said it anyway.) Long story short, a local saw me and fired at me, but thankfully the translator ran over and convinced the guys that the dude was just doing what he explained to me. It definitely didnt help relations all that much, but hopefully we can avoid stuff like that again. 

The National Guard guys have most of the island locked down now, and some construction guys are coming over here to begin setting up a base to really secure the island and start getting people to move in. Ill be able to see you once I get out of here though! I cant wait to show you the nice furnishing on this musket.

Love, your recently shot son, David.
MESSAGE STATUS: APPROVED AND SHIPPED

[/spoiler]

Official Statement from the Kingdom of Ekpatanus

To: The Republic of
Lavinsworth United Islands

Date: January 4, 2025

Subject: Declaration of Readiness for Cooperation and Assistance
In the name of God the Great
With best wishes for the progress and health of the National Guard of Lavinsworth, the Kingdom of Ekpatanus is proud to announce its readiness to provide any necessary infrastructural and military assistance to the beloved country of Lavinsworth.
We in Ekpatanus can take charge of the gas pipeline installation in the areas you have recently captured, ensuring that these regions are connected to the gas network in the shortest possible time. Additionally, in case of a shortage of weapons and military equipment, you can count on us.
Wishing victory and success for the National Guard of Lavinsworth and hoping for a close collaboration,
Kingdom of Ekpatanus
